item.content:encoded:
This was fine. Competently executed, and an alright idea. However, the strings of my heart were distinctly un-tugged.

Part of it, was the repetition between the interview logs (recalled in an intensely weird way for people who are prisoners being used as human guinea pigs) and the final documentation, with neither providing any additional information. There's also the, imo, rather pointless addendum, which adds nothing to the story.

My main issue is that struck me less as a wistful reminder of half-forgotten memories, and more as forced sentimentality. Maybe I've spent too long reading the comment sections for YouTube mixes with names like "I ' M S O A L O N E" and "N O S T A L G I C A T 2 A M"1 but my reaction to the memories was less "I will never get these moments back" and more "Oh, I have read this exact comment thirty times before."

I'm glad that this has been enjoyable for a lot of people, but I am not a fan. -1

Footnotes
1. Also, yes, this obviously pre-dates that whole genre of videos by several years, but I'm just trying to provide context my reaction.

item.content:encoded:
May I interest you in a spoiler this evening?
It arrives with a side of plot twist for your enjoyment.

Here were my initial thoughts:

There is a correlation between dosage and sleep time, but that gets wonky depending on how desperate the person is.

Generally if someone's at baseline-level happiness or higher, they'll sleep longer if they chug the entire bottle rather than taking a sip or two. I like to think that MC&D accounted for people who will use this as a sleep aid rather than a recreational drug. Take a sip before you go to sleep, and you'll still wake up in time for work and all that. Take two sips on the weekend maybe, and sweet dreams for longer.

The more desperate you are to return to the past, the more you'll sleep, regardless of the amount consumed.

But then I was all "nahhhh too complicated".

Basically, it comes down to yes, the Foundation making a mistake. The bit is there to make readers question it. The Foundation established the correlation (since it's been consistent over other trials, not listed in the excerpt), but it's only tentative until they can run further tests with consistent results.

item.title: Author's notes.
item.content:encoded:
This has gone through several stages of chat review; many thanks to Dmatix, Rumetzen, Woggle (almost forgot aaaa), Voct, Troy, and Mann in particular. I guess I’ll just note that when reading, keep in mind how the original owner of the SCP passed away, and what kind of people would be likely to use the SCP.

I came up with this idea based on a quote I heard once, “Peace of mind is the best sleeping pill.” The idea to walk away with here is basically, “It’s alright to escape to dreams, as long as you always wake up willing to face the world again.”

Spoilers, if you’ll have them.
hide

- Dosage has nothing to do with how long a person sleeps after consuming the liquid. Consecutive use does, to an extent.
- Someone who is just satisfied with their life, not necessarily totally happy with it, wouldn’t sleep much more than normal if they took a dose. Someone in a mid-life crisis might sleep for days on end.
- Taking a dose of the liquid multiple times is an act of giving in, of trying to escape. People will always look back fondly on the past, but one shouldn’t need something like this to do so.
- Someone who drinks from the bottle will experience memories exactly as they did the first time, not being able to think back on it or pass judgment on it until after they wake up.
- As indicated by the MC&D note, there definitely exist more instances of the bottle. A lot of people rely on it, but not everyone wakes up after each use.

Edit: The image belongs to me. The bottle pictured is a trinket I picked up while thrift shopping one day.
